angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 660,219 km at 81.05 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.3381 +/- 0.0166 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 81.05 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.949 +/- 0.006 solar radii from Jenkins et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LTT 9779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020NatAs...4.1148J/abstract): 660,219 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.02 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Jenkins et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LTT 9779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020NatAs...4.1148J/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5443 +/- 14 K from Jenkins et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LTT 9779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020NatAs...4.1148J/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Jenkins et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LTT 9779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020NatAs...4.1148J/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/ltt-9779.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.492, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
